outline.description: This chapter introduces the parties involved—including former congressman George Santos, comedian Jimmy Kimmel, ABC Television Network, and its parent Disney—and recounts how Kimmel used the Cameo platform to request personalized videos from Santos that were later aired on *Jimmy Kimmel Live!* as part of the "Will Santos Say It?" segment series.
subtopics: "Parties Identity" – Plaintiff’s status and Defendant entities
"Cameo Requests" – Mechanism by which Kimmel solicited videos
"Airing on JKL" – Broadcast context of the videos
"Complaint Filed" – Summary of factual allegations in SDNY filing
"Rule 12(b)(6) Dismissal" – District Court’s basis for striking all claims
"Appellate Review" – Second Circuit’s de novo standard per DiFolco

outline.chapter_title: II – Copyright Infringement Claims And Fair Use Defense
outline.description: This chapter examines Santos’s attempt to recover damages based on alleged infringement of his copyrighted personal videos and explains how the court applied §107’s four-factor fair‑use framework—highlighting purpose/character (transformative nature), nature of work, amount/substantiality, and market effect—to determine that the defense was dispositive even at the pleading stage.
subtopics: "§107 Overview" – Statutory framework governing fair use
"Purpose/Character Factor" – Transformative analysis versus original creator intent
"Nature Of Work Factor" – Classification between creative versus factual material
"Amount/Substantiality Factor" – Exactness in capturing videos published same day
"Market Effect Factor" – Lack (and definition) of economic harm or market substitution
"Bad Faith / Good Faith Argument" – Application (or lack thereof) from Harper & Row considerations
"Precedent Applications" – Hachette Book Grp., Andy Warhol Found., TCA Television Corp.
"District Court Conclusion" – Summary within first offense pat client objective
